title: Plan first: add pagination to a small API
goal: Add ?page and ?limit pagination to GET /items without breaking existing clients; the spec is at the top of tests/pagination.test.js. Step 1: get a plan from the agent in plan mode, with no code written. Step 2: critique it against the checklist and edit it (Claude Code: Ctrl+G). Step 3: save it as PLAN.md and commit it on its own. Step 4: have the agent implement from PLAN.md. npm test checks PLAN.md's structure and the pagination behaviour.
setup_cmd: D=~/fm-ex/ex-3-1-plan-first; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo "Already set up at $D. Run: cd $D (or delete it first to start over)."; else mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-3-1-plan-first/starter "$D" && cd "$D" && git init -q -b main && git add -A && git -c user.name=fm -c user.email=fm@example.com commit -qm baseline && npm install; fi

starter_prompts.claude: Enter plan mode first (/plan, or claude --permission-mode plan), then paste: Add pagination to GET /items. Read src/app.js and everything in tests/ first (tests/pagination.test.js is the spec; do not edit it). Produce a plan with these sections: Goal (and out of scope), Files to change, Steps, Risks and open questions (especially anything that breaks existing callers or handles invalid input), Verification. Ask me before assuming anything. After you approve the plan, tell Claude: Save the approved plan to PLAN.md and stop. Write no code.
starter_prompts.codex: Start a read-only session (codex -s read-only), then paste: /plan Add pagination to GET /items. Read src/app.js and everything in tests/ first (tests/pagination.test.js is the spec; do not edit it). Produce a plan with these sections: Goal (and out of scope), Files to change, Steps, Risks and open questions (especially anything that breaks existing callers or handles invalid input), Verification. Ask me before assuming anything. To save it, restart without -s read-only and say: Save the approved plan to PLAN.md. Write no code.

solution_notes: The plan is written before any code, and it names src/app.js as the only production file to change, so the diff can be checked against it.

It makes the backwards-compatibility decision explicit: the body stays a bare array, totals go in headers, and pagination only switches on when limit is sent. Changing the body shape would have broken every existing client.
Invalid input is specified in advance (400 with an error for bad or oversized limit and page, and for page without limit), and a page past the end returns an empty array.
Verification is concrete: the exact command, plus a manual curl check that the no-query response is unchanged.
